findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance check (and/or terraform test) that the rebar-mcp-serving-path-down alarm has an alarm_action wired to a human-reachable target, so a firing alarm actually notifies rather than only recording datapoints.
evidence: AC1: 'an unhealthy MCP upstream is detected and reported with an actionable signal. Verified by ... showing the alarm live on metric mcp_healthy'
Observed: 'A human reported it; nothing in the system could observe it.'
test_alarm_actions_terraform.py is described as covering 'the alarm guards, including the AWS description-length limit' — structural, not notification-delivery
findings.finding: The incident's defining failure was that 'nothing in the system could observe it' — a 12-hour silent outage a human eventually reported. AC1 verifies only that the alarm exists on metric mcp_healthy and that datapoints are published; neither the ACs nor the tests establish that the alarm ROUTES to a human/pager (an alarm_action) when it fires. An alarm with no notification target reproduces the original silent-outage failure mode while appearing 'live'.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC1's verification to assert the alarm's AlarmActions is non-empty and points at the operator notification channel (SNS topic / pager), and add that assertion to test_alarm_actions_terraform.py.
